steps.title: Closed
steps.caption: Closed: calls flow through to Service B while the breaker counts failures.
steps.body: In the normal **closed** state every call goes through to Service B. The breaker sits on the wire and records the outcome of each call.

steps.title: Failures pile up
steps.caption: Service B starts failing. Three failures in a row trip the breaker open.
steps.body: Service B starts timing out. Each failure bumps the breaker's counter; when it crosses the threshold (3 here, in practice usually a failure *rate* over a sliding window) the breaker **trips open**.

steps.title: Open: fail fast
steps.caption: Open: calls fail fast with a fallback, so Service B gets time to recover.
steps.body: While **open**, calls are rejected immediately instead of waiting for a timeout. Service A serves a fallback (cached data, a default, a friendly error) and Service B gets breathing room to recover.

steps.title: Half-open trial
steps.caption: Half-open: after the cooldown one trial call is let through; it succeeds, so the breaker closes.
steps.body: When the cooldown ends the breaker goes **half-open** and lets a single trial call through. It succeeds, so the breaker closes and resets its counter. Had it failed, the breaker would have gone straight back to open for another cooldown.
